simple.meaning: שַׁרְבִיט (sharbîyṭ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a rod of empire.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Esther 4:11. The surrounding context includes Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שַׁרְבִיט (H8275) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: שַׁרְבִיט (sharbîyṭ) / H8275 is traced through Esther 4:11, Esther 5:2, Esther 8:4 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “All the king’s servants, and the people of the king’s provinces, know, that whoever, whether man or woman, comes to the king into the inner court without being called, there is one law for him, that he be put to death, except those to whom the king might hold out the golden scepter, that he may live. I have not been called to come in to the king these thirty days.”
